title: Read the strace and say what is wrong

prereqs.why: The evidence is a syscall trace, and reading one is the skill being tested.
What the trace shows is the loader doing its search, so you need to know what it is searching for and where.

statement:
A colleague says a program "just exits immediately and prints nothing useful". You run it under `strace` and this is the tail of the output:

```
execve("./analyse", ["./analyse"], 0x7ffd1a2b3c40 /* 41 vars */) = 0
brk(NULL)                               = 0x55a3f8c21000
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/etc/ld.so.cache", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
fstat(3, {st_mode=S_IFREG|0644, st_size=78412, ...}) = 0
mmap(NULL, 78412, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE, 3, 0) = 0x7f2c1d4a1000
close(3)                                = 0
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libanalytics.so.2", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libanalytics.so.2", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
writev(2, [{iov_base="./analyse: ", iov_len=11}, {iov_base="error while loading shared libra"..., iov_len=43}], 2) = 54
exit_group(127)                         = 0
```

**What is actually wrong?**
hints: Look at which call failed and what it was trying to open. Notice there is no openat of the program's own data files anywhere in the trace.
`execve` returned 0, so the program was found and started. What runs between execve succeeding and main() being entered?
Exit status 127 is a specific convention. So is the fact that the error came out on fd 2 before any of the program's own work happened.

options: The dynamic loader cannot find `libanalytics.so.2`, so the program is killed before `main` ever runs.
The program lacks permission to read `libanalytics.so.2`, which is why the open returns an error.
The program crashed inside `main` while trying to open a data file it needs.
`/etc/ld.so.cache` is corrupt, which is why the subsequent opens fail.
